Building the AI Economy: What Happens After the Data Centre Peak

After peaking at US$212bn (2023 constant prices) in 2030, data centre construction work done is forecast to fall 40% by 2037 as new construction slows to the pace of long-run digital demand. y.

The future of data centre construction is set for significant shifts, with apeak forecasted at US$212 billion in 2030, followed by a 40% decline by 2037.This decline will vary across regions, with the Americas experiencing the mostsubstantial drop.

The Americas will peak last in 2030, maintaining elevated levels until 2032,primarily due to the lengthy construction of large campuses. In contrast, Asiawill peak in 2029, driven by a boom in Australia, while Europe is expected toplateau after peaking first in 2028, with Germany and the Netherlandscontracting post-2027.

As the construction landscape evolves, contractors in the US may face a sharpdecline in work after 2032, necessitating a shift in investment towards growingregions. The dynamics of market maturity, project types, and regulatoryenvironments will significantly influence the timing and depth of these regionalcycles.
